newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs and pork bellies end mixed.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs and pork bellies end mixed.

text.p: CME lean hog and pork belly futures ended mixed after rallying early from initial losses and slipping back late on continued concern over weakness in the cash pork complex, traders said.
Hogs closed 0.325 cent per lb higher to 0.300 lower with August off 0.250 at 79.850 cents. Pork bellies ended off 0.450 to up 0.900 cents with August up 0.075 at 78.500 cents.

Expectations of continued weak cash hog markets weighed on spot July hogs while fund rolling influenced trade in active August and October. Deferred months were narrowly mixed in light dealings, traders said.

Continued weakness in the cash pork product market should keep packer demand for hogs slow. This prompted selling that took futures down to technical support early before bouncing on short covering. Prices drifted back down late as demand lacked followthrough and fund rolling added to pressure in August, they said.
Much of the fund action was attributed to the start of the "Goldman roll", rolling of positions by Goldman Sachs for their commodity index, they added.

Fimat Futures USA, Refco and spread Cargill Investor Services long October/short August. R.J. O'Brien bought August after selling early against purchases by Rand Financials and locals short covering. Rosenthal Collins bought October late while Rand sold, pit sources said.
In hog options, commission houses sold October 78 calls while Refco sold October 72 and 78 puts, pit sources added.

Pork bellies also saw short covering support after initial carryover selling with the market appearing oversold after the recent 10 cent break and limit losses Monday. Selling was also lacking ahead of the out-of-town report, traders said.
Although the cash belly market continues to show weakness, expectations of a possibly large out-movement of frozen bellies from storage last week kept trade nervous into the close, they said.

Analyst estimates on the weekly CME out-of-town report ranged from out 750,000 lbs to 1.0 million lbs versus an out-movement of 1.179 million lbs and 1.85 million lbs out last year. However, pit traders are looking for an out-movement of 1.8 to 2.0 million lbs.
After the close, the CME reported a net out-movement of 1.541 million lbs last week.
This will likely have little effect on futures Wednesday as it is in the middle of both groups estimates, sources added.
R.J. O'Brien bought late while E.D.&F. Man and Smith Barney sold, pit sources said.
